_comment: Applied by seed.ts and the build_* scripts, GLOBALLY across all states (not MA-scoped despite the filename). junkPatterns are case-insensitive regex fragments matched against course name (test/admin/duplicate/non-golf ForeUp accounts). privateClubs are members-only MA clubs with no public tee times — excluded per 'public courses only'. Semi-private courses that sell public tee times are intentionally KEPT. `closed` (permanently closed) and `knownGap` (a public course we knowingly cannot cover) are reasoned exemptions read ONLY by scripts/audit_coverage.ts: a roster course listed here counts as reconciled instead of failing the coverage gate. Each entry is {name, reason}. 2026-07-08: removed the `^old ` junkPattern -- it was meant to catch 'Old Pakachoag Golf Course' (already separately excluded by exact id in duplicateIds), but as the roster expanded past MA it started wrongly killing legitimately-named courses like 'Old Tappan Golf Course' (NJ, a real town name, not a stale duplicate). Prefer exact duplicateIds over broad name-prefix patterns when the collision risk isn't MA-local. Also removed `tennis$` for the same reason: its real target (`ma-trull-brook-tennis`, a stale duplicate listing) is already covered by exact id in duplicateIds, but the bare regex was killing real golf-and-tennis clubs whose name legitimately ends in 'Tennis' (e.g. Colonial Golf & Tennis, PA) once the roster expanded past MA. 2026-07-08 (round 22): also removed the bare `\bspa\b` pattern for the same reason -- it was killing 'Grand Geneva Resort & Spa' (WI, real, live, verified). Unlike the two prior fixes, I couldn't confirm an exact duplicateIds entry this specific pattern was protecting against, but the more specific `club and spa` phrase pattern (still present, a few entries below) almost certainly covers whatever real junk case this was meant for, and a bare word-boundary match on 'spa' is exactly the kind of overly-broad pattern that keeps colliding with real golf resorts (spa amenities are extremely common at nicer courses) as the roster grows past MA.
